summary: Moel Famau, also spelled Moel Fama, is the highest hill in the Clwydian Range, on the boundary between Denbighshire and Flintshire in Wales. The hill gives its name to the Moel Famau country park and has been an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty since 1985. It is surrounded by several well-preserved Iron Age hill forts.
one_line: Moel Famau is the highest hill in the Clwydian Range on the Denbighshire–Flintshire border in Wales, known for its country park and Iron Age forts.
key_facts: Moel Famau (or Moel Fama) is the highest hill within the Clwydian Range.
The Clwydian Range was formerly known as the Flintshire Range.
Moel Famau lies on the boundary between Denbighshire and Flintshire in Wales.
The hill gives its name to the Moel Famau country park.
Moel Famau has been classed as an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty since 1985.
Moel Famau is surrounded by several well-preserved Iron Age hill forts.
